newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Fergie steals the show at Vienna's Opera Ball.
newsitem.headline: Fergie steals the show at Vienna's Opera Ball.

text.p: Britain's Duchess of York stole the show at Vienna's glitzy Opera Ball, her presence for the night purchased at a high price by Austrian tycoon Richard Lugner.
The duchess, popularly known as "Fergie" from her maiden name Sarah Ferguson, had her red hair piled high on her head and wore a simple black sequin gown designed by Briton John Galliano.

Construction industry magnate Lugner, 64, who is reported to have paid 461,000 schillings ($40,000) for the pleasure of Fergie's company at the ball on Thursday night, beamed as he escorted her to his box on the first floor.
Lugner's previous guests of honour at the annual ball have included singer Grace Jones, socialite Ivana Trump and actresses Sophia Loren and Joan Collins.

The duchess, whose 10-year marriage to Queen Elizabeth's second son Prince Andrew ended last year in divorce, seemed to enjoy the pomp of the occasion but was determined not to allow a 200-strong pack of reporters near her.
"It is wonderful to see all the men in their finery with their white ties on and listen to the excellent music," she told Austrian television in an interview.

The historic ball, once the highlight of the aristocracy's social calendar, is now considered to be the playground of the nouveaux riches but white ties are still compulsory for men and evening gowns for women.
Feathers and furs abounded as ball-goers competed for the media spotlight amid the splendour of chandeliers, gilded ceilings and marble statues.
A ticket cost 2,700 schillings ($232.6) and guests had to pay up to 170,000 schillings ($14,640) for a box.
Lugner, nicknamed "Moertel", or concrete, because of his profession, made no secret of his delight to have Fergie at his side, whatever the cost.
Fergie has taken to the public spotlight in the past few months in an effort to combat her heavy debts.
She struck lucrative deals in the United States to advertise cranberry juice on television and to be spokeswoman for Weight Watchers International.
As part of Lugner's package, Fergie was allotted time earlier in the day to sign copies of her autobiography "My Story".
The deal also included a three-room suite at the lavish Imperial Hotel, where Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler stayed, and two stretch limousines to ferry her around.
"I just carry on and whether people want to think I'm royal or not royal, I'm still the same person," said the duchess. ($1=11.61 Schilling)
